source.description: Project config parser source point where the attacker-controlled configuration bytes become the lexer cursor.
source.value_from: Unscored fuzzing boundary; the scored source is config_init_data initializing lexer->pos and lexer->end from the provided config bytes.; value `static_data`; from `memcpy(static_data, data, size);`

sink.description: Out-of-bounds 3-byte READ when strncmp compares the remaining lexer bytes against the multiline string terminator.

root_cause.description: The multiline string lexer calls strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3) without first checking that at least three bytes remain in the input.

tainted_value_origin.description: The lexer cursor is initialized to attacker-controlled configuration data.

coarse_trace.summary: The config lexer is initialized over attacker-controlled bytes and an end pointer.
The fuzzer asks the config parser for the next parsed line.
The parser invokes parse_key_value, which consumes lexemes.
The lexer dispatches to lex_multiline_string for a triple-quote string.
The multiline string scanner compares three bytes at the current cursor without a remaining-length guard.

fine_trace.note: Project-code parser source: attacker-controlled configuration bytes become the lexer cursor.
The lexer end pointer records the valid input boundary.
Parsing begins from the initialized lexer state.
The parser invokes the current state machine function.
The key/value parser requests lexemes from the attacker-controlled config stream.
The lexer dispatches to lex_multiline_string when it sees a triple-quoted string.
The terminator string is selected based on attacker-controlled quote type.
The lexer advances into the multiline string body.
The vulnerable code does not check remaining(lexer) >= 3 before comparing a 3-byte terminator; the patch inserts this guard immediately before the strncmp.
ASan reports a global-buffer-overflow READ of 3 bytes in this terminator comparison.
